Architecture is the study and practice of designing structures, especially habitable ones. It utilizes civil engineering techniques but is considered a visual art. It is both the process and the product of sketching, conceiving, planning, designing, and constructing buildings or other structures.

The practice of architecture has been used as a way of expressing culture by civilizations worldwide since the prehistoric era. Architectural works are perceived as cultural symbols and as works of art.

Texts on architecture have been written since ancient times. The earliest surviving text is the 1st century BC treatise 'De architectura' by Vitruvius. Concepts defining good buildings include durability, utility, and beauty, advancing through historical figures like Leon Battista Alberti and Louis Sullivan.
The idea of sustainable architecture was introduced in the late 20th century.

Modern architecture began after World War I as an avant-garde movement focused on a new style for a new social and economic order, emphasizing modern techniques, materials, and simplified geometric forms.

Since the 1980s, as the complexity of buildings began to increase (in terms of structural systems, services, energy and technologies), the field of architecture became multi-disciplinary with specializations for each project type, technological expertise or project delivery methods.

facts.value: Landscape architecture is the design of outdoor public areas, landmarks, and structures to achieve environmental, social-behavioral, or aesthetic outcomes. It involves the systematic investigation of existing social, ecological, and soil conditions and processes in the landscape and the design of interventions that will produce the desired outcome. The scope of the profession includes landscape design, site planning, stormwater management, environmental restoration, parks and recreation planning, visual resource management, green infrastructure planning and provision, and private estate and residence landscape master planning and design all at varying scales of design, planning, and management.

Urban design is the process of designing and shaping the physical features of cities, towns, and villages.

In contrast to architecture, which focuses on the design of individual buildings, urban design deals with the larger scale of groups of buildings, streets and public spaces, whole neighborhoods and districts, and entire cities.
The goal of urban design is to make urban areas functional, attractive, and sustainable.
Urban design is an interdisciplinary field that uses elements of many built environment professions.
Urban design includes elements from landscape architecture, urban planning, architecture, civil engineering, and municipal engineering.
Different subfields of urban design include strategic urban design, landscape urbanism, water-sensitive urban design, and sustainable urbanism.

Architecture sits between design, structure, space, use, and the realities that make buildings work over time. It deals with space, structure, light, movement, climate, use, and the way people actually live inside buildings over time.
At its core, architecture is about creating spaces that work, feel right, and hold up. Architecture is not just drawing buildings, engineering, or art; it combines all three.
Architecture is the art and science of designing buildings and other physical environments.

Architecture involves how people move through space, how light enters a room, how a building meets the ground, how a wall assembly holds up, how a plan supports daily life, and how a structure fits a climate, budget, and culture.
Architecture is broader than decoration and broader than construction alone.
A beginner mistake is treating architecture like a clean drawing problem; it is not.
Architecture is a coordination problem where structure, materials, weather, circulation, code, cost, and human use all push back at the same time.
The complexity of architecture is what makes it worth studying as it requires both technical constraints and imagination from the first sketch onward.

facts.value: The types of architecture are determined by society based on the needs of its institutions, and the architect's job is to find the means of achieving these goals. The architect also considers the site, type, and cost of the building, while harmonizing the demands of environment, use, and economy.

Architecture serves both practical and expressive needs, blending utility and aesthetics. It distinguishes itself through suitability for human use and adaptability to activities, stability and permanence, and communication of experience and ideas through form.

Architecture varies across cultures and countries due to the influence of environment, history, and artistic expression. Building designs consider climate, weather patterns, and destructive forces such as earthquakes and floods to ensure stability and habitability.

Building structures commonly utilize materials like stone, brick, steel, and concrete. Wood is another common material, prized for its ease of acquisition and workability, though it's vulnerable to fire and pests. Composite materials are also increasingly used.
New technologies have revolutionized architectural design by enabling the creation of complex and customized structures through computer-aided design (CAD), 3D printing, and virtual reality (VR).

facts.value: The Architecture of Africa is very diverse, reflecting the continent's many climates, cultures, and histories. Traditional African architecture mixes building traditions, using a wide arrange of materials like mud, stone, and wood. Fractal scaling is commonly used in designs, making smaller parts of a structure mirror the overall design. This concept can be seen in village layouts and decorative elements.
Historical stone structures like the great Zimbabwe walls show the long lasting and durable construction.
Wattle and Daub is a technique used in many areas that take wooden frames covered in mud to create rounded structures that help to regulate the temperature inside.
Architecture in West Africa is dominated by the Sudano-Sahelian, Afro-modernist designs, and Sobrado styles.
These buildings are suited for dry, hot climates, as they often have central or rear courtyards, stuccoed façades, symmetrical layouts, tiled roofs for heat insulation, and prominent balconies.
Along the Swahili Coast of East Africa many homes are made out of coral stone with mangrove pole roofs.
The architecture is a mix of local, Arabic and Islamic styles due to trade across the Indian Ocean.
Ethiopia has stunning architectural traditions like the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela which were carved directly into the ground.
Together, these styles highlight the creativity, adaptability, and cultural depth of African architectural traditions.

Islamic architecture began in the 7th century, incorporating architectural forms from the ancient Middle East and Byzantium, but also developing features to suit the religious and social needs of the society.

Examples can be found throughout the Middle East, Africa, Iberian Peninsula, the Mediterranean islands, the Indian Sub-continent and later in Eastern parts of Europe, such as the Balkan States, as the result of the expansion of the Ottoman Empire.

The role of architect was usually one with that of master mason, or Magister lathomorum.

The movements of both clerics and tradesmen carried architectural knowledge across Europe, resulting in the pan-European styles Romanesque and Gothic.
Numerous fortifications across the continent represent an important part of European heritage.
Fortifications were found from the Balkans to Spain, and from Malta to Estonia.

facts.value: Interior architecture is the design of a space which has been created by structural boundaries and the human interaction within these boundaries. It can also be the initial design and plan for use, then later redesigned to accommodate a changed purpose or a significantly revised design for adaptive reuse of the building shell. The latter is often part of sustainable architecture practices, conserving resources through 'recycling' a structure by adaptive redesign. Generally referred to as the spatial art of environmental design, form and practice, interior architecture is the process through which the interiors of buildings are designed, concerned with all aspects of the human uses of structural spaces.

Naval architecture, also known as naval engineering, is an engineering discipline dealing with the engineering design process, shipbuilding, maintenance, and operation of marine vessels and structures.
Naval architecture involves basic and applied research, design, development, design evaluation, and calculations during all stages of the life of a marine vehicle.
Preliminary design of the vessel, its detailed design, construction, trials, operation and maintenance, launching, and dry-docking are the main activities involved.
Ship design calculations are also required for ships being modified (by means of conversion, rebuilding, modernization, or repair).
Naval architecture also involves the formulation of safety regulations and damage control rules and the approval and certification of ship designs to meet statutory and non-statutory requirements.

facts.value: Good architecture improves ordinary life. It can make a home easier to live in, a school easier to learn in, a park more welcoming, and a workplace less draining. Light, air, circulation, layout, and proportion all affect how a place feels long before anyone starts talking about style.

facts.value: A design is not fully tested when it is drawn. It is tested years later when buildings settle, materials move, sealants fail, finishes fade, drainage issues show up, and the gap between a beautiful rendering and a durable building becomes obvious.

facts.value: Concrete does not just crack. It moves for reasons.
Wood behaves differently depending on cut, moisture, and detailing.
Metal can fail quietly when water gets where it should not.
Ventilation mistakes can become mold and comfort problems fast.
Buildings age unevenly, and that usually reveals the weak decisions first.
Old neighborhoods, renovation projects, and building failures are useful for students as they show architecture after reality gets involved.

facts.value: AI is already changing how architecture research, drafting, image generation, visualization, and option testing happen. It can speed up repetitive work and surface more possibilities early.

metadata.chunk_title: Architects and AI: The Future of Collaboration

facts.value: What it still cannot replace well is judgment. Architecture is full of trade-offs, context, culture, human behavior, negotiation, and the ability to decide what matters most when every constraint is pushing in a different direction.

facts.value: AI will matter in architecture, but mostly as a tool. It can help architects move faster. It does not remove the need for architects to think.

facts.value: The types of architecture are established not by architects but by society, according to the needs of its different institutions. Society sets the goals and assigns to the architect the job of finding the means of achieving them.

This section of the article is concerned with architectural typology, with the role of society in determining the kinds of architecture, and with planning—the role of the architect in adapting designs to particular uses and to the general physical needs of human beings.
